artist.name: Lyn Lapid
artist.short_description: Maryland-raised singer-songwriter blending intimate pop stories with alternative R&B and jazz-influenced phrasing.
artist.biography: Lyn Lapid is an American singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist who grew up in Maryland. She studied classical instruments before attracting a large online audience through covers and her original song 'Producer Man' in 2020. Its story of pressure to compromise her artistic identity helped establish the personal voice of her early work. She subsequently released 'In My Mind' and the 2022 EP 'The Outsider', before developing a relationship narrative across 'to love in the 21st century' and its extended 'epilogue' edition in 2023. Discussing the project in a 2024 interview, Lapid described broadening a storyline about romantic ambiguity to include the friendships that support someone through it. Her debut album 'BUZZKILL' followed in April 2025. In an interview surrounding that release, Lapid tied the album to moving to Los Angeles, struggling to connect socially and eventually understanding that belonging does not require pleasing everyone. She gave specific explanations for 'floater friend', 'back up plan' and the album title track. Afterglow describes her work as emotionally observant indie pop with alternative R&B touches; these are editorial style labels, not an assertion that her entire catalogue fits a single genre. Her profile broadens Afterglow from romantic heartbreak into themes of friendship, identity and early-adult self-discovery.
